Q91a.rule: QLever-lane performance evidence (P1, P4, P5, GS) counts only from a server whose data sits mostly in a built base index with a delta bounded by a declared rebuild threshold. Every QLever receipt records base triple count, delta triple count and the delta in the blocks the measured scans touched. The lane's design (R2, R8, R13, R17) always assumed this; nothing built or measured it, and qlever-dev's base holds 1 triple. Earlier QLever latency numbers from delta-only servers are DIAGNOSTIC.

Q91b.rule: qlever-dev is no longer reset with --fresh as a delta policy; delta growth on shared residents is handled by the rebuild loop of Q91c once it is qualified.

Q91c.rule: EXP-QG1 (lab/experiments/EXP-QG1-qlever-generations/) builds the rebuild loop: phase 1 on an exclusive slot measures scan and join cost against delta size (monotonic and spread keys) on a 10M-triple base and picks the threshold; phase 2 rebuilds blue/green index generations from the broker log, with reader leases so one multi-request read stays on one generation, and checks Q89i byte identity across every swap. The feed stays the log. Bounding the delta per graph is rejected (all graphs share one server's blocks).

Q91d.rule: The first rebuild-index runs on a copy of qlever-dev's data on an exclusive slot, not on the shared resident, because several reviews read qlever-dev live and upstream bug #3172 can make a rebuild fail.

Q93a.rule: For seed reuse on every lane, the only evidence that grants admission is a content fingerprint (G0) read through the engine by the process that will measure, on the endpoint it measures, before its warm-up, compared with a digest pinned before the freeze began (and with O-DOMAIN where one exists). Every other observation (stop, settle, log tails, frontiers, inspect, stderr, timers, owner state, copy hashes, plan hashes, disk) is refusal-only or a diagnostic, and no decision reads a diagnostic.

Q93b.rule: Fields, pinning point and counts as in sections 2.1 and 3.2; every read has a deadline; the golden is published only after two starts of a clone each reproduce `D` and the layout digest `L`.

Q94b.rule: Every GS stream is W0-valid and every domain claim a scenario names is checked by O-DOMAIN; a scenario whose spec names a domain claim and whose run makes no such check fails closed. The W01 world vocabulary is retired

Q94c.rule: The GS background is the frozen TARGETS 2.1 trace through the W0 trace mapper (Q92k); the private writerTrace is retired; every measured window holds one burst and one maintenance event

Q94d.rule: GS world admission follows Q93a: a G0 content fingerprint per run; a fresh scope or verified clone per run; store counts at start and end; on lane Q the Q91a counts

Q94e.rule: Every GS receipt before contract 0.4.0 is DIAGNOSTIC: none closes an obligation or enters a comparison. The GS.12 defect and the W01b harness findings stay as defect reports

Q94f.rule: GS.04b applies only to compositions with a separate current store; on those it is required. GS.04's engine-kill schedule is required on every lane and runs only on an exclusive slot

Q94g.rule: GS.19's outbox and GS.10's publications must be the product's atomic outbox; a harness-side outbox file can pass only GS.19's P3 checks, as a diagnostic
Q94g.basis: R37 g; TARGETS 3 (atomic path to the outbox); Q42c

Q94h.rule: GS.10's race (in-flight reconciles finish on the old release) is scheduled as EXP-P5 round C, right after rounds A and B, and is required for GS.10 to close

Q93c.rule: G0 admits a clone by the full digest D over every stored column (byte-level identity with its golden). E1, which compares a clone with a fresh seed of the same inputs, uses a second digest D' over the same columns with engine-assigned values normalized: engine-generated ids and system timestamps are replaced by their rank in commit order, and every other column is kept as is. A fresh seed must match the golden's D', never its D. The normalization list is part of the G0 module, each entry with a comment naming the engine source that assigns it, and a test fails if a column is normalized without one.

Q83d.rule: Settle evidence does not require observing L0 tries: compaction may merge them before the first poll. Settled means the new block's tx_id and latest_processed_msg_id equal the node gauges, xt.trie_stats covers that block at whatever level it now sits, compactor jobs 0, and the file listing and trie digest are unchanged over three readings 5 s apart.
Q83d.basis: K01 round 2 (G3 blocked by fast compaction)

Q83e.rule: Settle evidence records three values separately and never equates them: (a) the block-cut frontier F, the immutable block's latest_processed_msg_id; (b) the settled replay frontier M, the processed watcher after maintenance drains (lag 0, jobs 0, tries stable, over the Q83d polls); (c) the stable application transaction T. F < M is accepted only when every source message in (F, M] is read from the stopped log tail and is a maintenance message (TriesAdded, compactor output), never an application transaction; T is unchanged across the window. The final stopped log tails and the reference and clone resume are bound to M. Exact reference/clone equality and the two-start catalog checks stay. This replaces the part of Q83d that refused every F < M.
Q83e.basis: XTDB c6c1962: BlockCutter.kt:235, 280-295; SourceMessage.kt:139-147; Compactor.kt:150-152; SourceLogProcessor.kt:142, 199-211; Database.kt:375-387
